props: Use case: style-transfer. Redraw a Korean village RPG object atlas with EXACTLY 3 columns x 3 rows on a square transparent canvas. Image2 supplies ONLY the existing objects and layout, NOT its overly detailed rendered texture or thick black outlines. The new assets must look like low-resolution hand-placed 16-bit game pixels, not painterly illustrations. Use 1 logical pixel THIN COLORED outlines (dark blue for roofs, dark brown for wood, dark green for foliage), never a thick black sticker border. Clear large flat color areas, only 2-3 shades per material, no tiny texture noise, no gradients, blur, glow, smooth diagonals or 3D rendering. Logical buildings about64x64pixels, props32x32 or32x48pixels, visibly square pixels enlarged cleanly. Muted slate-blue giwa roofs, warm timber brown, pale cream walls, sage/olive green, teal water-related accents. Preserve Korean hanok style and overhead RPG front view. Exactly9 isolated objects centered within equal cells, broad transparent gaps at least48pixels, no overlap: row1 laboratory hanok with small telescope; guardian hall hanok with restrained green/red dancheong and PLAIN WOOD above doorway, absolutely NO FLAG NO TAEGEUK NO SYMBOL; hanok shop with simple cream awning and onggi jar. Row2 compact hanok home; coastal pine tree; low stone flower planter. Row3 short capped stone wall; small Korean coastal research boat top-down with bow UP, simple cream hull wood deck and slate blue cabin, NO FLAG; roofed wooden noticeboard with blank cream panel and two posts. Simplify roof tiles into rhythmic square pixel shapes, windows into sparse lattice, leaves into a few large pixel clusters. Do not include people, text, labels, ground patches or shadows. Keep all9 objects fully visible on transparent alpha.
terrain: Use case: stylized-concept. A production pixel-art TERRAIN texture atlas matching the attached small Korean RPG character's simple 16-bit square-pixel style. OPAQUE landscape image, exact 3 columns x 2 rows, SIX equal square swatches with NO gutters, borders, labels, text, padding or divider lines. Entire canvas filled edge to edge. Each swatch is a uniform repeatable TOP-DOWN GROUND TEXTURE, not an isolated object, no perspective, no terrain cutaway. Each swatch logical32x32pixels enlarged with crisp square pixels, only3-4flat shades, subtle low-contrast patterns, no black outlines, no gradients, no photorealism. Row1 left: calm desaturated teal coastal water, sparse tiny softly colored pixel ripples, avoid bright foam or big waves. Row1 middle: short sage green grass lawn, sparse subtle olive grass tufts, mostly flat ground. Row1 right: denser tall grass field of small rounded olive-green blade clusters on the SAME sage base, clear but not noisy, grass all points upward, no individual outlined bushes. Row2 left: sandy warm-beige village path with sparse flat grey-beige small stepping stones embedded, mostly beige ground, no large cobblestones. Row2 middle: pale warm sand shore with a few low-contrast ochre grain pixels, no shells or rocks. Row2 right: warm-brown wooden pier decking seen straight down, horizontal parallel planks, restrained grain, no rails or poles. Texture edges should join seamlessly with copies of the same texture; no shading or vignette near edges. Common restrained palette of sage, olive, muted teal, ivory, warm grey and timber brown. Very quiet ground textures so characters remain readable. No buildings, characters, ships, flags or symbols.
